questions.stem:
The Venn diagram shows the probabilities of customer bookings at Harry's hotel.

$R$ is the event that a customer books a room

$B$ is the event that a customer books breakfast

$D$ is the event that a customer books dinner

$u$ and $t$ are probabilities.

[Venn diagram: $R$ and $B$ are overlapping ellipses inside $D$'s overlapping ellipse; the region in $B$ only is $0.33$, the region in $R \cap B$ (inside both $B$ and $D$'s overlap with $R$) is $0.27$, the region in $R \cap D$ only is $0.15$, the region in $R$ only (outside $B$, inside $R \cap D$ boundary) is labelled $u$, the region in $D$ only (outside $R$) is labelled $t$, and the region outside all three circles is $0$.]

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down the probability that a customer books breakfast but does not book a room.
(1)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that the events $B$ and $D$ are independent
(b) find the value of $t$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\mathrm{P}(B) = 0.27+0.33 = 0.6$, $\mathrm{P}(D) = 0.27+0.15+t$, $\mathrm{P}(B \cap D)=0.27$
M1: for attempting 3 suitable probabilities, one involving $t$ (at least 2 correct); e.g. sight of $0.6, 0.27, 0.42+t$ correctly labelled in terms of $B,D,R$ or in a correct equation. May see e.g. $\mathrm{P}(B|D)=\frac{0.27}{0.42+t}$
[$\mathrm{P}(B)\times \mathrm{P}(D) = \mathrm{P}(B \cap D)$ gives] $0.6\times(0.42+t)=0.27$
M1: for using the independence to form a linear equation in $t$. ft their probs if stated.
$0.42+t=\frac{0.27}{0.6}$ or $0.6t=0.018$
A1: for solving leading to a correct equation as far as $p+t=q$ or $pt=q$
$t=0.03$
A1: for $0.03$ or exact equivalent

parts.label: c
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) [$u=$] $1-(0.6+0.15+t)$
M1: for a correct expression for $u$. Allow their $t$ or just letter $t$ in a correct expression
$u=0.22$
A1ft: for $0.22$ (or exact equivalent) or ft their $t$, provided $u$ and $t$ are probs. Can score M1A1ft provided their $u$+their $t$=$0.25$ where $u$ and $t$ are both in $[0,1]$

parts.label: d
parts.mark_scheme:

M1: for a correct numerical ratio of probabilities
$=0.45$
A1: for $0.45$ or exact equivalent (Answer only 2/2)
(ii) $\left[\frac{\mathrm{P}(D \cap [R \cap B'])}{\mathrm{P}(R\cap B')}\right] = \frac{0.15}{0.15+u}$
M1: for a correct numerical ratio of probabilities, ft their $u$, provided $u$ is a probability
$=\frac{15}{37}$
A1: for $\frac{15}{37}$ or $0.\dot{4}0\dot{5}$ or allow awrt $0.41$ following a correct expression (Answer only 2/2)

parts.text:
A coach load of 77 customers arrive at Harry's hotel.

Of these 77 customers

40 have booked a room and breakfast

37 have booked a room without breakfast

(e) Estimate how many of these 77 customers will book dinner.
(2)

questions.stem:
A midwife records the weights, in kg, of a sample of 50 babies born at a hospital. Her results are given in the table below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Weight } (w \text{ kg}) & \text{Frequency (f)} & \text{Weight midpoint } (x) \\ \hline 0 \leqslant w < 2 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline 2 \leqslant w < 3 & 8 & 2.5 \\ \hline 3 \leqslant w < 3.5 & 17 & 3.25 \\ \hline 3.5 \leqslant w < 4 & 17 & 3.75 \\ \hline 4 \leqslant w < 5 & 7 & 4.5 \\ \hline\end{array}$

[You may use $\sum fx^2 = 611.375$]

A histogram has been drawn to represent these data.

The bar representing the weight $2 \leqslant w < 3$ has a width of 1 cm and a height of 4 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Calculate the width and height of the bar representing a weight of $3 \leqslant w < 3.5$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Width $= 0.5$ (cm)
B1
e.g. 4 [cm$^2$] represents 8 babies or frequency densities are 8 and 34
M1: for clear representation of area with frequency or height$\times$width$=8.5$
Height $= 17$ (cm)
A1: for 17 (cm) [Must be clear it is height not frequency] (Ans only must satisfy $h\times w = 8.5$)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use linear interpolation to estimate the median weight of these babies.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $[Q_2=]$ $\{3\}+\frac{(25-9)}{(26-9)}\times 0.5$, or $\{3.5\}-\frac{(25-24)}{(41-24)}\times 0.5$
M1: for $\frac{16}{17}\times 0.5$ or if using $n+1$ for $\frac{16.5}{17}\times 0.5$. May see $-\frac{1}{17}\times 0.5$ if working down
$=$ awrt $3.47$ (allow $\frac{59}{17}$)
A1: for awrt 3.47 (or $\frac{59}{17}$) [check from correct working] or (if using $(n+1)$ for) 3.485 or awrt 3.49

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) (i) Show that an estimate of the mean weight of these babies is 3.43 kg.
(ii) Find an estimate of the standard deviation of the weights of these babies.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c)(i) $\sum fx = 1\times 1+2.5\times 8+3.25\times 17+3.75\times 17+4.5\times 7=171.5$, $\bar{x}=\frac{171.5}{50}=(3.43)$ (*)
B1cso: for $\sum fx$ (at least 3 correct \& no incorrect products seen) and correct $\frac{\sum fx}{50}$ or $\frac{171.5}{50}$
(ii) $\sqrt{\frac{611.375}{50}-3.43^2}$
M1: for a correct expression including square root. Must use 3.43 no ft
$=0.680147\ldots$ (awrt 0.680)
A1: for awrt 0.680 (accept 0.68). Allow use of $s=$ awrt 0.687 (Ans only 2/2)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Shyam decides to model the weights of babies born at the hospital, by the random variable $W$, where $W \sim \mathrm{N}(3.43, 0.65^2)$

(d) Find $\mathrm{P}(W<3)$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $[\mathrm{P}(W<3)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z<\frac{-0.43}{0.65}\right)]=\mathrm{P}(Z<-0.6615\ldots)$
M1: for an attempt to standardise with 3, 3.43 and 0.65. Allow $\pm$ and also use of their sd
$=1-0.7454$ (tables)
M1: for $1-p$ where $0.74<p<0.75$ NB calculator gives 0.7458665...
$=0.2546$ awrt 0.254~0.255
A1: for awrt 0.254 or 0.255

parts.label: e
parts.text:
(e) With reference to your answers to (b), (c)(i) and (d) comment on Shyam's decision.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) (b) and (c)(i) mean $\neq$ median or skew or mean$\approx$median or no skew and comment
B1: for a statement about mean/median and compatible comment about normal
(d)$=0.254$ or $0.255$ compare data$=0.18$ (or $12.7$ compared with $9$)
B1: for statement comparing their (d) with data (sight of 0.18 or 12.7 and 9 required)
0.18 different from 0.25 so normal not good or 0.18 similar to 0.25 so normal is OK
dB1: dep on 2nd B1 for conclusion about normal compatible with 2nd statement

parts.label: f
parts.text:
A newborn baby weighing 3.43 kg is born at the hospital.

(f) Without carrying out any further calculations, state, giving a reason, what effect the addition of this newborn baby to the sample would have on your estimate of the
(i) mean,
(ii) standard deviation.
(3)

B1: for no change in mean {send a correct argument for decrease to review}
(ii) s.d. will decrease (Extra value is at "centre" so data more concentrated)
B1: for s.d. decreases

Both statements correct and correct reasons for each

questions.stem: The time, in minutes, taken by men to run a marathon is modelled by a normal distribution with mean 240 minutes and standard deviation 40 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the proportion of men that take longer than 300 minutes to run a marathon.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) [$T \sim \mathrm{N}(240,40^2)\ldots$ require $\mathrm{P}(T>300)$]
$\mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{300-240}{40}\right)$
M1: for standardising with 300, 240 and 40. May be implied by use of 1.5. Allow $\pm$
$=1-\mathrm{P}(Z<1.5)$ or $1-0.9332$
M1: for $1-\mathrm{P}(Z<\text{"1.5"})$ i.e. a correct method for finding $\mathrm{P}(Z>\text{"1.5"})$ e.g. $1-p$ where $0.5<p<0.99$
$=$ awrt $0.0668$ or $6.68\%$
A1: for awrt 0.0668 (Answer only 3/3)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Nathaniel is preparing to run a marathon. He aims to finish in the first 20% of male runners.

(b) Using the above model estimate the longest time that Nathaniel can take to run the marathon and achieve his aim.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $[\mathrm{P}(T<n)=0.20 \Rightarrow]$ $\frac{n-240}{40}=-0.8416$
M1: for an attempt to standardise with 240, 40 and $n$ and set $=\pm z$ ($0.8<|z|<0.9$)
B1: for $z=\pm 0.8416$ (or better) used as a $z$ value. Do not allow for $1-0.8416$. Calc gives $0.8416212\ldots$ [May be implied by awrt 206.34, give B1 as well as A1 if seen]
$n=$ awrt $206$ minutes

Ans only: If answer is awrt 206 score M1B0A1 (unless of course $z=0.8416$ seen) but awrt 206.34 scores 3/3

The time, $W$ minutes, taken by women to run a marathon is modelled by a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ minutes.

Given that $\mathrm{P}(W<\mu+30)=0.82$

(c) find $\mathrm{P}(W<\mu-30\mid W<\mu)$
(3)

$=0.36$
